overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique shorts indicates clear polarization: first-person hypothetical space survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic paradoxes consistently reach 800-1,000+ views with healthy engagement (up to 3.7% like rate). In contrast, generic psychology snippets ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and repeated uploads ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') suffer severe viewer fatigue, languishing under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Peril / Extreme 'What If You Fell Into...' Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) significantly outperform third-person trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme astronomical and planetary phenomena as immediate, visceral first-person survival scenarios.

winning_patterns.pattern: High-Contrast Cosmic Paradoxes & Extreme Value/Sensory Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views, published most recently on Oct 1), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,027 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies' (723 views) drove peak velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Leverage impossible physics, extreme wealth values, or paradoxical planetary conditions in the title and opening 3 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved only 5 to 53 views across three separate variations; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' capped at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire passive cognitive trivia unless embedded inside a high-stakes psychological mystery or survival narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 220 to 34 views; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' plateaued.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict fresh-topic filters; never re-upload verbatim concept hooks that showed declining trajectory.
